subproblem.title: Iterated blow-ups of a zero-scale limit at a point of the unit ball are again zero-scale limits of blow-ups of T (the (IBL) membership step)
subproblem.statement: Assume (IBL) — verbatim the frozen type of the registered dependency iterated_blowup_limit of the grandparent node blowup_class: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ U, x_i → x, λ_i > 0 with λ_i → 0, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), y ∈ ℝ^P, s_k > 0 with s_k → 0 and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P): if there are δ > 0 and Γ with M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all x′ ∈ B_δ(x) and 0 < ρ < δ, blowUp T x_i λ_i ⇀ S and blowUp S y s_k ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly), then there is a strictly increasing φ with blowUp T (x_{φ(k)} + λ_{φ(k)}•y) (λ_{φ(k)}s_k) ⇀ C. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), z ∈ ℝ^P, r ∈ ℝ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), points c_i ∈ ℝ^P and scales t_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ), and b ∈ U, such that dist(c_i, z) < r − t_i for every i, t_i → 0, c_i → b, blowUp T c_i t_i ⇀ S in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), and there are δ > 0 and Γ ∈ ℝ with M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and 0 < ρ < δ. Let y ∈ ℝ^P with ‖y‖ < 1, s_k > 0 (k ∈ ℕ) with s_k → 0, and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with blowUp S y s_k ⇀ C. Then there are points c′_k ∈ ℝ^P and scales t′_k > 0 (k ∈ ℕ) such that dist(c′_k, z) < r − t′_k for every k, t′_k → 0, c′_k → b and blowUp T c′_k t′_k ⇀ C.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the class-membership step 'ν ∈ 𝓜' of cases (ZS-i) and (ZS-ii) of the parent's supplied proof (Simon 7.3.3, proof of (1), chapter-07.txt lines 443–486: a tangent cone of a member of 𝒯₀ is again in 𝒯₀ because η_{y,s#}η_{x_i,λ_i#}T = η_{x_i+λ_iy, λ_is#}T). Here C is arbitrary; in the parent C is a tangent cone of S at y, or the zero current.
1. (Iterated limit.) Apply (IBL) with P, n, U (open), T, x := b ∈ U, xs := (c_i), lams := (t_i) (positive), S, y, ss := (s_k) (positive) and C. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumptions: c_i → b, t_i → 0, s_k → 0, the mass bound at b with (δ, Γ), blowUp T c_i t_i ⇀ S and blowUp S y s_k ⇀ C. It gives a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with blowUp T (c_{φ(k)} + t_{φ(k)}•y) (t_{φ(k)}s_k) ⇀ C.
2. (A tail with small scales.) Since ‖y‖ < 1, the number 1 − ‖y‖ is positive, so {s ∈ ℝ : s < 1 − ‖y‖} is a neighbourhood of 0. As s_k → 0, there is k₀ ∈ ℕ with s_k < 1 − ‖y‖ for all k ≥ k₀.
3. (New data.) For k ∈ ℕ put i(k) := φ(k + k₀), c′_k := c_{i(k)} + t_{i(k)}•y and t′_k := t_{i(k)}·s_{k+k₀}. Then t′_k > 0 as a product of two positive numbers.
4. (The admissibility inequality.) Fix k. Since t_{i(k)} > 0, dist(c′_k, c_{i(k)}) = ‖t_{i(k)}•y‖ = t_{i(k)}‖y‖. By the triangle inequality and the assumption dist(c_{i(k)}, z) < r − t_{i(k)},
 dist(c′_k, z) ≤ dist(c′_k, c_{i(k)}) + dist(c_{i(k)}, z) < t_{i(k)}‖y‖ + r − t_{i(k)} = r − t_{i(k)}(1 − ‖y‖).
 Since k + k₀ ≥ k₀, step 2 gives s_{k+k₀} < 1 − ‖y‖, so t_{i(k)}(1 − ‖y‖) > t_{i(k)}s_{k+k₀} = t′_k (t_{i(k)} > 0). Hence dist(c′_k, z) < r − t′_k.
5. (Limits of the data.) The map k ↦ k + k₀ tends to ∞ (tendsto_add_atTop_nat), and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ tends to ∞ (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop); hence i(k) → ∞. Therefore t_{i(k)} → 0, c_{i(k)} → b and s_{k+k₀} → 0. It follows that t′_k = t_{i(k)}·s_{k+k₀} → 0·0 = 0 (Tendsto.mul) and c′_k = c_{i(k)} + t_{i(k)}•y → b + 0•y = b (Tendsto.add, Tendsto.smul_const).
6. (Weak convergence.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) be a test form. By step 1, currentEval(blowUp T (c_{φ(k)} + t_{φ(k)}•y) (t_{φ(k)}s_k)) ω → C(ω). Composing this real sequence with k ↦ k + k₀ (which tends to ∞) gives a sequence with the same limit, and its k-th term is currentEval(blowUp T c′_k t′_k) ω: the centres and scales agree, and the proofs of nonvanishing of the scale inside blowUp are irrelevant (proof irrelevance). Hence currentEval(blowUp T c′_k t′_k) ω → C(ω) for every ω, i.e. blowUp T c′_k t′_k ⇀ C.
Steps 3–6 show that (c′_k), (t′_k) satisfy all requirements: t′_k > 0, dist(c′_k, z) < r − t′_k, t′_k → 0, c′_k → b and blowUp T c′_k t′_k ⇀ C. ∎
proof_key_steps: (IBL) at x := b with the data (c_i, t_i), S, y, (s_k), C gives a strictly increasing φ with blowUp T (c_{φ(k)} + t_{φ(k)}y) (t_{φ(k)}s_k) ⇀ C.
Choose k₀ with s_k < 1 − ‖y‖ for all k ≥ k₀ (s_k → 0 and ‖y‖ < 1).
Put c′_k := c_{φ(k+k₀)} + t_{φ(k+k₀)}y and t′_k := t_{φ(k+k₀)}s_{k+k₀} > 0; the triangle inequality gives dist(c′_k, z) < r − t_{φ(k+k₀)}(1 − ‖y‖) < r − t′_k.
t′_k → 0 and c′_k → b, and the tail k ↦ k + k₀ of the weakly convergent sequence of step 1 converges weakly to C.
